pages: Tam Rooke, a farm man of fifty-six, grey at the temples in a brown work coat with rolled sleeves, crouches at the stone ring and lifts one dry pine stick off the hot stones. Middle distance: a barrow of pine, the two iron bars. Background: the valley village and the beck at still evening. Warm flame light from below, cold blue dusk behind.

Ollie Coe, a farmer of forty-four, dark hair going grey at the sides in a blue work shirt with sleeves shoved up, stands at the washing line with both hands hooked over the rope above his head, leaning into it. Middle distance: one wet sheet, the ring stones. Background: the valley village, May dusk. Fading daylight, the fire lifting behind him.

Ivy Marlow, eighty-one, white hair under a black shawl, stands at the washing-line post with one hand laid flat on the wood, speaking. Middle distance: the flame up over the iron bars, a lit sheet. Background: the ring at the village centre, dusk in May. Orange light thrown from below onto her face.

Nell Rooke, sixteen, dark braided hair in a scarlet-red coat, leans over the bar of her barrow of wet sheets and looks down at the ring of stones. Middle distance: the flame settled a hand above the stones, a hanging sheet. Background: the ring, the washing line, Friday in July, late afternoon. Low warm light, one long shadow on the stones.

Nell Rooke, sixteen, dark braided hair in a scarlet-red coat, stands at the washing line with a wet sheet held open in both hands, looking across the ring. Middle distance: the low flame burning knee high inside the stones, a white enamel washboard. Background: the ring, the beck path, a Wednesday in June. Quiet light, the flame barely touching the stones.

Ollie Coe, forty-four, dark hair, in a white shirt and brown waistcoat soaked at the shoulders, stands under the propped shuttered window and looks down at the stripe of rain steaming on the stones. Middle distance: the flame, high for daylight, and two poles holding the window. Background: the ring at a wedding, rain, late June. Grey wet light with the fire burning through it.

Ollie Coe, forty-four, wet dark hair, in a white shirt and brown waistcoat with his collar open, stands up on a flat stone at the ring with one hand lifted, speaking. Middle distance: the flame rising past the iron bars, a shuttered window on two poles. Background: the ring, rain stopping, late June evening. Warm firelight climbing his face against the wet grey.

Tam Rooke, fifty-six, grey at the temples in a wet brown work coat, kneels inside the stone ring and lowers one armful of split pine onto the embers. Middle distance: a cone of blackened wet wood, a barrow. Background: the ring in the village, driving rain, August afternoon. Dull grey daylight, the flame barely visible under the stones.

Nell Rooke, sixteen, dark braided hair soaked flat in a scarlet-red coat gone dark at the shoulders, takes a sheet from a bundle and looks straight at the ring. Middle distance: the low flame barely clearing the stones, a white enamel washboard. Background: the washing line in the rain, the beck running, a Tuesday in August. Flat wet light, drips off the rope.

Nell Rooke, sixteen, dark braided hair in a scarlet-red coat buttoned to the throat, stands with her back to the flame at the iron bars, one sleeve pressed to her face. Middle distance: the fire up over the bars, a sheet peg in her hand. Background: the ring above the village, an October afternoon after a burial. Deep orange light from behind her.

Nell Rooke, sixteen, dark braided hair under a grey shawl over her scarlet-red coat, stands at the ring in falling snow and looks down into the stones. Middle distance: a small blue bead of flame, a white enamel washboard. Background: the washing line strung over the ring, December noon, the valley grey. Cold even light, no shadow thrown.

Ollie Coe, forty-four, dark hair, in a heavy dark green coat thrown open, stands at the ring at night with one palm flat on an iron bar. Middle distance: the flame driving up past the bars, long shadows down the village. Background: the washing line and the sleeping village, eleven at night, January. Hard orange light from below, dark blue night.

Nell Rooke, sixteen, dark braided hair in a scarlet-red coat, stands at the ring with a bundle of school sheets against her chest and turns her head up the path. Middle distance: a blue flame barely above the stones, a white enamel washboard. Background: the ring and the path to the Pyke house, a cold morning in January. Pale flat daylight, no shadow thrown.

Nell Rooke, sixteen, dark braided hair in a scarlet-red coat, holds a rough white feed sack over one shoulder and stands at the line with her chin lifted, speaking. Middle distance: the flame steady at a foot, a wet sheet in her hands. Background: the ring, the beck, an afternoon in January. Warm light on her face, shadow behind.

Nell Rooke, sixteen, dark braided hair in a scarlet-red coat, the rough white feed sack at her feet, stands at the ring looking up into a flame a foot high. Middle distance: the iron bars, the wet stones around the fire. Background: the washing line, the beck, late January morning. Steady warm light, long shadow cast back from the flame.

Ollie Coe, forty-four, dark hair, in a dark green coat with a paper held out in one hand, stands at the ring at eight in the morning. Middle distance: the flame up over the bars, frost on the stones. Background: the wall and the beck, the second week of February, hard frost. Clear cold light with warm fire against it.

Ollie Coe, forty-four, dark hair, a blue work shirt with the sleeves rolled, lays an axe down in the wet grass at the edge of the stone ring. Middle distance: the fire, steady and tall, a heap of sacks. Background: the stone ring and the beck, the last week of April, windy. Wind light, warm fire glow on the grass.

Ollie Coe, forty-four, dark hair, sleeves rolled in a blue work shirt, stands at the line with one hand holding out a corner of his own wet sheet. Middle distance: the axe lying in the grass, the flame burning high and steady. Background: the ring, the beck, a windy last week of April. Bright moving light, long shadows off the fire.
